content.text:
Welch Allyn / Hillrom / Baxter makes several **ophthalmology and eye-exam tools**, especially handheld diagnostic instruments. Common options include:

| Tool | What it’s for | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **PanOptic Plus Ophthalmoscope** | Direct fundus/retinal exam | Current wide-view Welch Allyn model; includes “Quick Eye” alignment to help direct patient gaze. ([hillrom.com](https://www.hillrom.com/en/products/panoptic-plus-ophthalmoscope/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **3.5 V Coaxial Ophthalmoscope** | General eye exam/fundus viewing | Uses Welch Allyn coaxial optics to help reduce glare and improve entry into the eye. ([hillrom.com](https://www.hillrom.com/en/products/3-5v-coaxial-ophthalmoscope/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Prestige Coaxial-Plus Ophthalmoscope** | Higher-end direct ophthalmoscopy | Features coaxial optics, Halogen HPX illumination, and 68 focusing lenses. ([hillrom.it](https://www.hillrom.it/en/products/prestige-coaxial-plus-ophthalmoscope/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **AutoStep Coaxial Ophthalmoscope** | Direct ophthalmoscopy with step lens changes | 3.5 V model with 68 lenses in single-diopter steps. ([hillrom.ca](https://www.hillrom.ca/en/products/3-5v-autostep-coaxial-ophthalmoscope/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Streak Retinoscope** | Objective refraction | Often paired with an ophthalmoscope in 3.5 V diagnostic sets. |
| **Ophthalmic Sets** | Bundled handles + heads | Welch Allyn sets may include the PanOptic Plus ophthalmoscope and/or retinoscope depending on configuration. ([hillrom.com](https://www.hillrom.com/en/products/ophthalmic-sets/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **PocketScope Ophthalmoscope** | Portable/basic eye exams | Smaller, student-friendly/pocket format; less capable than full 3.5 V systems. ([hillrom.com](https://www.hillrom.com/content/dam/hillrom-aem/us/en/marketing/products/pocketscope-ophthalmoscope/documents/PocketScope%20Operating%20Instructions%2C%20User%20Manual%2C%20Multi-language.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |

If you’re **buying for medical/PA/nursing school**, a **PocketScope or basic ophthalmoscope/otoscope set** may be enough unless your program specifically requires a 3.5 V set. If you’re in **optometry/ophthalmology or doing frequent eye exams**, consider a **3.5 V Coaxial**, **PanOptic Plus**, or a **retinoscope + ophthalmoscope set**.

If you tell me your use case—**student, clinic, optometry, ophthalmology, primary care, or replacement parts**—I can narrow down the best Welch Allyn option.
